newsitem.title: USA: Cash crudes choppy against steady U.S. outrights.
newsitem.headline: Cash crudes choppy against steady U.S. outrights.

text.p: Differentials for cash crude prices in the U.S. Gulf firmed Tuesday morning on jitters over when Iraqi crude will return to market, and refiner ratable buying, dealers said.
Outright prices returned to the steady level after popping higher on reports the Exxon Baytown, Texas refinery was struck by lightning Monday, forcing a 110,000 FCC unit down for a short duration.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was steady at $19.75-85 a barrel, with October outrights around 4-6 cents firmer at $19.80-90 a barrel.
Gasoline futures continued to lead the crude market, rolling to higher prices on bullish fundamentals showing strong demand, traders said.

Deals in September grades saw Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sell at a 23 cents premium to the WTI/Cushing, Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at 20 cents under benchmark and Midland/WTI at a 30 cents discount.

Sour barrels were sold as strong as a $1.25 discount to the marker, in some 20 cents from the start of the week. Traders said refiners in need of filling ratable barrel needs propelled prices, along with "panic" buying on concerns over when Iraqi sour crudes would return.
"There were refiners in there buying in panic on reports the Iraqi crude would be delayed into August later than they thought," said a crude player.

Positioning buys on when and if Baghdad is allowed to sell oil again has become the center of market focus, traders said. The U.N. is still reviewing an aid distribution plan for possible approval by the end of the week. If there are no delays after the plan's approval, Iraqi oil could be lifted by the middle of August, traders said.
Still, it is not certain who will pick-up the Iraqi crude and if the term deals seen for the oil deal's first round can be duplicated this time.
